name: soma-pub-auth
description: Sign-in, for every identity provider on one channel (§I). `{provider}` in the route picks the entry: `/v1/auth/github` begins GitHub's grant, `/v1/auth/google` a directory's, and the callback comes back to `/v1/auth/{provider}/callback`. GitHub is carried in `providers` here because it is OAuth2 (no id_token) and needs a userinfo fetch and a custom identity map, which only a channel block can hold; `providers_from_instance` merges the deployment's `[oauth2_login.providers.*]` (a Google, an Entra, a Keycloak -- an OIDC issuer discovers its own endpoints), so a tenant adds a directory with no change here. Orion owns the 302, the signed state cookie and its CSRF binding, PKCE, the code exchange and, for an OIDC provider, id_token verification, and hands the workflow a NORMALISED identity at `metadata.identity` -- one upsert on (provider, subject) serves them all. The one route with a rate limit of its own rather than public_rate: it mints a session, so it is limited per address and far harder than a read. No auth block, because presenting one is what it is for.
